title: Comme dans The Revenant  (Like in The Revenant)

segments.t: Andrea plays confidential video rushes of Jean Dujardin acting like a feral beast in the wilderness. Producer Maxime watches in horror as Andrea compares Dujardin's extreme performance to Leonardo DiCaprio in The Revenant. Let's listen to the scene in French first.
La réalisatrice crie que la prise est coupée!
Jean continue de jouer malgré l'ordre d'arrêter.
Mais qu'est-ce qu'il mange dans cette scène?
Il est comme un vrai démon sauvage!
C'est à la hauteur de DiCaprio dans The Revenant.
Attends, cet animal sauvage est bien réel?
Oui, ce lapin est un vrai lapin sauvage.
Il mange un animal cru devant la caméra?
Jean s'est totalement transformé pour ce grand rôle.
C'est trop fou pour notre comédie familiale, Andréa.
Alors dis-moi enfin où se cache Jean Dujardin.
Il prend simplement quelques jours de repos mérité.
Je veux le voir demain dans mon bureau!
Let's examine how Maxime reacts to Dujardin's shocking performance step by step to explore extreme method acting.
La réalisatrice crie que la prise est coupée!

'The director is shouting that the take is cut!' Maxime watches the monitor as the director tries in vain to stop filming. This conversational past tense combines a helper verb with the past verb form for 'cut!'.
Jean continue de jouer malgré l'ordre d'arrêter.
'Jean continues to act despite the order to stop.' Andrea shows that the star was too deeply immersed to hear. Notice how 'continues' leads directly into the noun meaning 'the command'.
Mais qu'est-ce qu'il mange dans cette scène?
'But what is he eating in this scene?' Maxime squints at the disturbing action on screen. The verb meaning 'what is it' pairs naturally with the noun for 'scene?' in everyday conversation.
Il est comme un vrai démon sauvage!
'He is like a true wild demon!' Andrea describes the fierce, untamed power of the actor's performance. The key noun here means 'demon', anchored by its matching French article.
C'est à la hauteur de DiCaprio dans The Revenant.

'It is right up there with DiCaprio in The Revenant.' Andrea compares the role to famous Hollywood survival drama. Notice how the short vowel drops before a vowel sound around 'it is', making the phrase flow smoothly as one unit.
Attends, cet animal sauvage est bien réel?
'Wait, is this wild animal truly real?' Maxime asks with growing disgust whether prop effects were used. Notice how 'wait' leads directly into the noun meaning 'animal'.
Oui, ce lapin est un vrai lapin sauvage.
'Yes, this rabbit is a real wild rabbit.' Andrea reveals that no special effects were involved. The descriptive adjective for 'real' agrees in gender and number with its noun.
Il mange un animal cru devant la caméra?
'He eats a raw animal in front of the camera?' Maxime cannot believe the star went to such shocking lengths. The descriptive adjective for 'raw' agrees in gender and number with its noun.
Jean s'est totalement transformé pour ce grand rôle.
'Jean has totally transformed for this great role.' Andrea defends total immersion as the mark of a great artist. Notice how 'has' leads directly into the noun meaning 'role.'.
C'est trop fou pour notre comédie familiale, Andréa.
'That is too crazy for our family comedy, Andrea.' Maxime worries that a feral star will ruin his mainstream movie. The descriptive adjective for 'crazy' agrees in gender and number with its noun.
Alors dis-moi enfin où se cache Jean Dujardin.

'So tell me finally where Jean Dujardin is hiding.' Maxime demands the actor's immediate whereabouts. The short 'self' word sits right in front of the verb for 'tell me', turning the action back onto the subject.
Il prend simplement quelques jours de repos mérité.

'He is simply taking a few days of well-deserved rest.' Andrea tries to downplay the actor's ongoing breakdown. The verb meaning 'is taking' pairs naturally with the noun for 'days' in everyday conversation.
Je veux le voir demain dans mon bureau!

'I want to see him tomorrow in my office!' Maxime delivers a firm ultimatum before walking out. The verb meaning 'want' pairs naturally with the noun for 'office!' in everyday conversation. Now let's listen to the scene once more from start to finish.

That's it for this scene around like in the revenant. When you watch the episode, listen out for the expressions meaning 'director' and 'shouts'. You'll catch them now. See you next time!
À demain!
